At the crossroads of empires, Romania’s history has been shaped as much by geography as by politics. The lands of modern Romania were once part of the Roman province of Dacia, conquered in the 2nd century AD. The Latin linguistic legacy remains visible today in the Romanian language — a Romance language surrounded by Slavic-speaking neighbors. After the Roman withdrawal, the region became a frontier contested by migrating peoples and later by powerful empires, including the Ottoman, Habsburg, and Russian. In the 19th century, Wallachia and Moldavia united, laying the foundation for a modern Romanian state. Independence from the Ottoman Empire was secured in 1877–1878, and after World War I, Romania expanded significantly in what became known as “Greater Romania.” The 20th century brought authoritarian rule, territorial losses during World War II, and later decades under communist leadership, most notably under Nicolae Ceaușescu. The 1989 revolution ended communist rule and opened a new chapter. Since then, Romania has pursued integration into Western institutions, joining NATO and the European Union. Its history reflects resilience at a geopolitical crossroads — shaped by conquest, adaptation, and reinvention across centuries. #meme #politics #usa #iran #europe

It starts with a girl sharing some positive traits—like the fact that she doesn’t drink or party—which immediately wins over a group of guys holding red balloons. This sets off a chain reaction of dramatic “combat” scenes where the guys use slow-motion movements and exaggerated expressions to mimic a battlefield. Even when one friend is “taken down” (falling gently to the floor after his balloon pops), the rest of the group continues the play-fight with incredible energy. The highlight is the finale, where a “soldier” appears with a massive cardboard prop, leaving everyone—including the girl—in a state of hilarious shock. Artificial intelligence continues to revolutionize the job market and how we work. Educators across Duke are being challenged to train students on how to use AI and prepare for careers that will increasingly depend on the technology. But the Fuqua School of Business is going beyond just incorporating AI in the curriculum, with its new experiments using AI systems in the classroom to assess student performance. Here’s how it works: Fuqua classrooms are already equipped with cameras and microphones that record classes using Panopto, a video management system that then makes recordings available to students. Students generally check in to class using a Bluetooth and NFC-based “Fuqua Checkin” app. Under the new system, students would check in to class by scanning NFC tags at their seats, which then associates their student information with that seat. This information would be used in conjunction to additional microphones with the capability of ascertaining the exact position of speakers in the classroom. Transcripts are fed to an in-house AI system that "objectively" grades participation by assessing comment relevance and whether statements spur conversation. While framed as innovation, this transforms the classroom from a space of intellectual risk-taking into a monitored performance arena where spontaneity, vulnerability and genuine learning become casualties of surveillance. The system illuminates just how artificial intelligence could change the practice of education. Scott Dyreng, senior associate dean of Innovation at Fuqua and the champion of this technology, claims that the system enables greater feedback for students and instructors alike. Read more at the link in bio. ✍️: Shezaz Hannan 📸: Alex Long

AI tutoring is what allows this incredibly bright student to work at the *exact* pace and level he needs. This is why I’m such a staunch advocate for integrating safe, effective, and thoughtfully designed AI technology into education. Because without it, this 99th percentile student would have been held back a grade for no reason. When learning lacks customization and personalization, the majority of kids suffer. I argue that less than half of kids in a given class are following at the exact same speed the teacher is going. The rest are straggling behind or speeding ahead. It’s time for adults to wake up and pull our heads out of the sand. Technology will only continue to advance, and it’s up to us to use it for the good of our kids. What does this actually look like in practice, you ask? Every morning at the 20+ locations of the schools I co-founded, students are working on academics for only 2-3 hours each day. When each student goes at their own speed with their own 1:1 tutor, they’re able to condense the whole school day into just a couple of hyper-focused hours. By the way, we’re not just letting them loose with Chat GPT or Gemini. Our team of developers work extremely hard to build this learning science principled AI-powered technology. The rest of the day is then dedicated to life skills workshops. The balance between academic mornings and life skill afternoons, peppered with lots of short breaks and close adult guidance, means our students are set up to avoid burnout entirely and nurture their natural love of learning. ❤️

Clavicular — whose online persona is KingClavicular — is one of the most controversial and fast-rising figures in the streaming world. He’s known not for his gaming skill, but for something more provocative: his unapologetic focus on looks-maxing, self-improvement, and aesthetics. What first gained him traction was his TikTok fame: raw confidence, sculpted looks, and an aura of self-optimization. On Kick, Clavicular’s streams mix “Just Chatting”-style IRL energy with deeply personal discussions around appearance upgrades, self-image, and confidence. He doesn’t shy away from controversial or taboo topics — whether that’s unlicensed cosmetic tweaks, look-enhancement philosophy, or his views on ideology. What sets Clavicular apart is how intimately he involves his audience in his self-improvement journey. Much like Asmongold’s candid commentary draws people in, Clavicular’s openness about his routines, his “glow-up” philosophy, and even risky cosmetic experiments make his streams feel like a live experiment — one that observers can’t stop watching. That said, his rise hasn’t been without storm. He made headlines when a clip showed him injecting fat-dissolving peptides into his underage girlfriend — sparking backlash over ethical, legal, and safety concerns. This controversy has raised serious questions about boundaries, responsibility, and the influence of self-optimization culture on impressionable audiences. Yet despite (or maybe because of) the drama, his audience is deeply engaged. Clavicular has built a loyal following not just interested in “how to look good,” but in why look matters so much in modern internet culture. He’s become a lightning rod — someone who embodies the extremes of self-improvement trends, making people think, debate, and reflect. In short, Clavicular isn’t just a streamer. He’s a provocateur, a self-optimization evangelist, and a polarizing personality. Born in 1949 in Tel Aviv, he grew up partly in the United States and later served in the elite Sayeret Matkal unit of the Israeli Defense Forces. Before entering high-level politics, he worked in business and diplomacy, including serving as Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations in the 1980s. He is known for his strong stance on national security, opposition to Iran’s nuclear program, and support for expanding Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Over the years, he has built close relationships with several international leaders and has played a major role in regional agreements, including normalization deals between Israel and some Arab nations. His career has also been marked by controversy. Netanyahu has faced corruption charges, which he denies, and his leadership has sparked both strong support and significant opposition within Israel. Supporters view him as a tough and experienced leader focused on security and economic growth, while critics argue that his policies have deepened political divisions and strained democratic institutions.

Tel Aviv, officially known as Tel Aviv-Yafo, stands as Israel's vibrant economic, technological, and cultural hub along the Mediterranean coast, roughly 60 kilometers northwest of Jerusalem. Founded in 1909 as a modern Jewish suburb on sandy dunes north of the ancient port city of Jaffa, it has grown into a dynamic metropolis that blends youthful energy with deep historical layers. The city proper has a population of around 495,000 to 502,000 people, while the broader Gush Dan metropolitan area, often referred to simply as greater Tel Aviv, now approaches 4.64 million residents in early 2026, reflecting steady urban expansion and making it home to a significant portion of Israel's population.What sets Tel Aviv apart is its distinctive character as the "city that never stops" - a secular, liberal, and cosmopolitan place often called the "Bubble" or the "Non-Stop City." Unlike the more religiously intense and historically weighted Jerusalem, Tel Aviv embraces a hedonistic, forward-looking lifestyle centered on sun-soaked beaches, world-class food, thriving nightlife, and an unapologetically progressive vibe. Its long stretch of golden Mediterranean beaches forms the heart of daily life, where locals and visitors alike jog, play matkot (beach paddle tennis), swim, or simply relax year-round under the blue sky, with the city's skyline of modern towers rising dramatically behind the shore.

Tel Aviv, officially known as Tel Aviv-Yafo, stands as Israel's vibrant economic, technological, and cultural hub along the Mediterranean coast, roughly 60 kilometers northwest of Jerusalem. Founded in 1909 as a modern Jewish suburb on sandy dunes north of the ancient port city of Jaffa, it has grown into a dynamic metropolis that blends youthful energy with deep historical layers. The city proper has a population of around 495,000 to 502,000 people, while the broader Gush Dan metropolitan area, often referred to simply as greater Tel Aviv, now approaches 4.64 million residents in early 2026, reflecting steady urban expansion and making it home to a significant portion of Israel's population.What sets Tel Aviv apart is its distinctive character as the "city that never stops" - a secular, liberal, and cosmopolitan place often called the "Bubble" or the "Non-Stop City." Unlike the more religiously intense and historically weighted Jerusalem, Tel Aviv embraces a hedonistic, forward-looking lifestyle centered on sun-soaked beaches, world-class food, thriving nightlife, and an unapologetically progressive vibe. Its long stretch of golden Mediterranean beaches forms the heart of daily life, where locals and visitors alike jog, play matkot (beach paddle tennis), swim, or simply relax year-round under the blue sky, with the city's skyline of modern towers rising dramatically behind the shore.
